title: Errors by service and type
prompt: The on-call dashboard lists each kind of error per service: how often it happened and when it last did. Write `solve(error_events)` with pair RDD functions so it returns `service`, `error_type`, `errors` and `last_seen`.
rules: One row per combination of `service` and `error_type`. The same error type in two services gives two rows.
`errors` counts the events, repeated ones included. `last_seen` is the latest `occurred_at`.
An event with no `occurred_at` still counts, but can't be the latest; if no event of a combination has a time, `last_seen` is missing.
hints: A key can be a tuple: `((service, error_type), value)`.
Carry `(1, occurred_at)` as the value and combine two values into `(count, later time)`.
Python's `max` can't compare a `datetime` with `None`. Write a small `later(a, b)` that returns the other one when one is missing.
explanation: Key each event by the tuple `(service, error_type)` with the value `(1, occurred_at)`, then `reduceByKey(lambda a, b: (a[0] + b[0], later(a[1], b[1])))`, where `later` skips a missing time. Flatten `((service, type), (n, last))` into four values and use `toDF` with a schema string. Keying by `error_type` alone merges types that two services share, `min` gives the first time instead of the last, and plain `max` fails on a missing time.
